papers.title: Bidirectional links between food intake and sleep: a naturalistic mobile EEG study
papers.summary: This naturalistic study used mobile EEG and questionnaires to examine bidirectional links between sleep and food intake in healthy participants. Results indicate that the timing of meals and sleep is reciprocally associated, while sleep quality or composition showed no negative effect after large, late, or satiating last meals.

papers.title: Working memory operations emerge from dynamic changes in neural subspace geometry
papers.summary: Using M/EEG in a working memory task, the authors found that neural subspace geometry flexibly reshapes with task demands: prioritization expands subspaces while de-prioritization shrinks them, and subspaces become more orthogonal under high cognitive demands. These changes were driven by interactions between aperiodic activity and delta/theta oscillations.

papers.title: Decision Confidence Neuron in Echo State Network for Continual Evaluation of EEG Motor Imagery Classification Quality
papers.summary: The paper proposes an explicit decision-confidence readout neuron for Echo State Networks to continuously monitor confidence during decision formation. In EEG-based motor imagery classification, confidence activity increased with decision accuracy and discriminated correct from error decisions, particularly in higher-performing participants.

papers.title: Exploratory deep-learning-driven early risk stratification of significant neurological injury in pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
papers.summary: This study developed a multimodal deep-learning framework using clinical variables and EEG spectral features to predict significant neurological injury (SNI) in pediatric ECMO patients. The clinical-only model achieved the highest AUC of 74.29%, and adding EEG features did not significantly improve performance, with clinical variables being the main contributors.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of EEG microstates during postural control in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: The study examined EEG microstate dynamics during a virtual-reality postural-control task in early-stage Parkinson's disease (PD) patients compared to healthy controls. PD patients showed increased duration and coverage of microstates A and B, and altered transition probabilities, suggesting candidate task-state EEG microstate alterations.

papers.title: Heart Rate Variability During Short-Term Electroencephalography.
papers.summary: This study measured heart rate variability (HRV) from single-channel ECG during short-term EEG in 103 patients with normal EEG results. HRV was reduced compared to normal values, particularly the high frequency band, and remained stable across wakefulness and sleep stages, suggesting that routine HRV measurement during EEG could provide prognostic information.

papers.title: Sleep spindle state-dependent motor cortical plasticity induction by EEG-triggered ripple burst TMS
papers.summary: The study investigated sleep spindle state-dependent plasticity induction using EEG-triggered ripple burst TMS in sleeping healthy participants. Spindle-trough rTMS led to consistent long-term depression-like changes in corticospinal and sensorimotor cortical excitability, unlike other spindle states.

papers.title: Differential modulation of sensorimotor alpha rhythms by motor imagery, electrical stimulation, and mirror visual feedback following peripheral nerve reconstruction: an EEG study.
papers.summary: This study compared EEG sensorimotor rhythm modulation during motor imagery (MI), electrical stimulation (ES), and ES combined with mirror visual feedback (MVF) in patients after peripheral nerve reconstruction and healthy controls. Alpha suppression was evident during ES and MVF in patients but not during MI alone, suggesting multimodal rehabilitation may facilitate cortical reorganization.

papers.title: Impact of a Multisensory Intervention: An EEG-based Spectral Analysis.
papers.summary: This study used EEG spectral analysis to objectively assess the effects of a multisensory room intervention in healthy controls, individuals with cerebral palsy (CP), and traumatic brain injury (TBI). Significant pre-post differences in alpha band power and alpha/beta ratio were found in healthy controls and CP groups, suggesting relaxation, while TBI showed non-significant qualitative trends.

papers.title: Thalamocortical network dynamics can explain visual impulse responses and perceptual echoes.
papers.summary: The paper characterizes visual responses in marmoset V1 to broadband flicker, finding non-oscillatory stimulus-locked dynamics and sparse steady-state spiking. A thalamocortical network model explains these dynamics and, when damping is reduced, reproduces oscillatory alpha-band dynamics seen in human impulse responses, suggesting a role for thalamocortical alpha resonance in perceptual echoes.

papers.title: Altered alpha-band regulation during naturalistic theory of mind processing in autistic children.
papers.summary: EEG was recorded from autistic and typically developing children viewing an animated film to examine alpha-band activity during theory-of-mind scenes. Typically developing children showed increased alpha power in right temporoparietal junction and prefrontal cortex during theory-of-mind processing, while autistic children did not, suggesting altered neural regulation in autism.

papers.title: Model-based cardiac field artefact correction for OP-MEG.
papers.summary: The authors developed a model-based method to correct cardiac field artefacts in OP-MEG recordings by estimating the cardiac dipole moment and using head rotation to separate cardiac and brain signals. Simulations and a single-participant proof-of-principle show that the method can correct sensor-level artefacts under dynamic head movement.

papers.title: The Expression and Effects of Rev-Erbα in Different Cerebral Regions of Mice With Acute and Chronic Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This study examined the circadian regulator Rev-Erbα in acute and chronic epilepsy mouse models. Its expression was dysregulated, and activation with SR9009 reduced seizures, abnormal EEG discharge, and improved behavioral outcomes, suggesting antiepileptic and neuroprotective effects.

papers.title: Late cross-modal biases in neural spatial representations revealed by EEG decoding.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: The study used EEG decoding to track spatial representations during an audiovisual ventriloquist task. Cross-modal biases emerged only after ~200 ms, with auditory representations biased earlier than visual, suggesting that multisensory integration occurs via late feedback processes.

papers.title: The effects of deep TMS on QEEG power, asymmetry, and coherence metrics in major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: Resting-state QEEG measures were assessed before and after 36 sessions of deep TMS in 75 MDD patients, yielding an 82.6% response rate and significant symptom reduction. Post-treatment, left prefrontal delta power decreased, frontal beta asymmetry shifted leftward, and coherence between left prefrontal and temporal lobes improved, indicating neurophysiological changes related to treatment.

papers.title: Periodic EEG: clinical settings, in vitro models, and potential mechanisms.
papers.summary: This review examines periodic EEG complexes in pathological conditions, categorizing contexts into infections, hypoxic/ischemic events, and metabolic disorders, and discusses potential cellular mechanisms including altered excitation-inhibition, metabotropic glutamate receptor activation, and electrical coupling, with testable predictions linking these mechanisms to anticonvulsant drug responsiveness.

papers.title: A U-shaped relationship between perceived chronic stress and the approach motivation: evidence from resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: In 60 undergraduates, perceived chronic stress showed U-shaped quadratic relationships with resting EEG measures of approach motivation: alpha frontal asymmetry, delta power, and theta power were enhanced at both low and high stress levels but reduced at moderate stress. Results suggest a nonlinear link between chronic stress and approach motivation.

papers.title: Characteristics of EEG activity in soccer players' alerting effects under different cues.
papers.summary: This event-related potential study compared alerting effects between elite soccer players and novices. Elite players showed faster reaction times, higher alerting network scores, larger N1 amplitudes, and smaller P2 amplitudes, indicating enhanced neurophysiological alerting function associated with soccer expertise.

papers.title: Gamma and Beta Neurofeedback Training Can Improve Visual Perception With Spectral and Regional Specificity.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial, gamma and combined gamma-beta neurofeedback training improved visual perception in healthy adults. Both groups showed increased parieto-occipital gamma, while central beta increased only in the gamma-beta group, and improvements were linked to enhanced evidence accumulation.

papers.title: Exploring EEG and ECG in Music Listening: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review examined 18 peer-reviewed studies using simultaneous EEG and ECG during passive music listening in healthy adults. Findings were heterogeneous and lacked integration, highlighting methodological inconsistencies and a need for standardized guidelines to study brain-heart interactions in music.

papers.title: Exploratory definition of a clinically meaningful change in intracranial EEG features: Analysis of data from a long-term treatment study of the RNS® System.
papers.summary: This post hoc analysis of data from a long-term RNS System treatment study sought to define a clinically meaningful change in intracranial EEG long episode frequency. A threshold of ≥30% LE reduction was associated with a ≥50% reduction in clinical seizures, supporting LE as a biomarker.

papers.title: Psilocybin-induced changes in electroencephalography link acute and long-term effects.
papers.summary: In a double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial, psilocybin acutely reduced alpha/beta power and increased gamma diversity, returning to baseline by 6 hours. At 24 hours, reduced delta/theta power correlated with positive life changes at 4 weeks, independent of acute psychological effects.

papers.title: A systematic review of electrophysiological markers of reward processing in addiction.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 42 studies examined electrophysiological markers of reward processing in substance and behavioral addictions, focusing on anticipation and outcome phases. Altered neural responses were observed across multiple stages in both addiction types, but methodological heterogeneity limited conclusions.

papers.title: Respiratory Support With Nasal High Flow Reduces Opioid Requirements During Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial compared nasal high flow to low-flow oxygen during ERCP under sedation. NHF reduced opioid requirements while maintaining ventilation and oxygenation, with no adverse events, suggesting it is a promising modality for procedural sedation.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Functional Network Responses to Immersive Virtual Reality in Alzheimer Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: Exploratory Single-Session 3-Group Repeated-Measures Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study examined EEG functional network changes during immersive VR exposure in 60 older adults with Alzheimer disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and normal cognition. It found higher global efficiency and modularity in AD at baseline, but no significant differences during VR, suggesting state-dependent network modulation.

papers.title: Sex-dependent cortical responses to terpene-based olfactory stimulation revealed by EEG and sLORETA.
papers.summary: This study investigated cortical responses to terpene-based aromas (orange and pine) using EEG and sLORETA in males and females. It found sex-dependent changes: orange increased beta/gamma power in males, whereas pine increased beta power in females, with distinct cortical activation patterns.

papers.title: Confounding by indication and the "low yield" of continuous EEG in paediatric severe traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: This letter discusses confounding by indication and the low diagnostic yield of continuous EEG in pediatric severe traumatic brain injury, addressing potential biases in research on nonconvulsive seizures.

papers.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined With Electroencephalography Analysis Suggest Time-Dependent and Region-Specific Modulation of Cortical Excitability During Acute Alcohol Intoxication.
papers.summary: This exploratory study assessed cortical excitability changes during acute alcohol intoxication using TMS-EEG in 34 adults. Amplitude of TMS-evoked potentials (P30, N45, P60, P180, N100) decreased at 30 min and partially recovered by 120 min, with regional specificity in frontal and central regions.

papers.title: Improving career guidance accuracy through EEG-based vocational interest assessment and self-reported RIASEC profiles.
papers.summary: The study compared vocational interest profiles from self-reported RIASEC assessments with EEG-based neurometric profiles in 33 participants, finding strong overall convergence but meaningful discrepancies leading to different occupational recommendations. EEG-based neurometrics may complement traditional self-report measures by capturing less explicit vocational preferences.

papers.title: Education Research: Online EEG Learning Platforms for Resident and Fellow Education.
papers.summary: This scoping review characterized 15 publicly accessible online EEG learning platforms for residents and fellows, finding variable functionality and gaps in pediatric/neonatal content, EEG manipulation, personalized feedback, and program integration. The findings support using online platforms for foundational instruction within hybrid curricula.

papers.title: A group brain-controlled method for UAVs using a hybrid paradigm of hand movements and visual evoked potentials.
EEG Analysis of Visual Attention Under Perception of Affective Prosody in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG theta/beta ratio during visual attention tasks with affective prosody in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and typically developing controls. ASD group had higher TBR overall, and temporal TBR differed between happy and sad prosody under high load, suggesting emotion-cognition interactions.

papers.title: Epilepsy Is Part of the CNS Phenotype in Classic Infantile Pompe Disease.
authors: Johanna M P Van Den Hout
papers.summary: In an international study of 17 patients with classic infantile Pompe disease, epilepsy was found to be part of the CNS phenotype, with seizures typically occurring after age 7, variable semiology, and associated with white matter abnormalities and cognitive impairment. The findings suggest the need for seizure risk evaluation during follow-up.

papers.title: Pragmatic Phenotype-Electrophysiology-Genomics Integration in Pediatric Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes: Insights From 36 Patients in a Single-Center Study in China.
papers.summary: This single-center study of 36 pediatric congenital myasthenic syndrome patients revealed high genetic heterogeneity, frequent variants of uncertain significance, and improved outcomes with genotype-informed therapy, though CHAT-CMS was associated with higher ventilator use and early mortality. Integrating phenotype, electrophysiology, and genomics supports diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: A novel method for obtaining epileptic brain tissue for omic analyses using electrodes from a clinical stereoelectroencephalography study
papers.summary: This study describes a method to extract brain tissue from stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) electrodes for transcriptomic and proteomic analysis. Using samples from six epilepsy patients, they obtained high-quality RNA and protein and found inflammatory markers most pronounced in the epileptogenic zone.

papers.title: Combination of stereo-electroencephalography and electrocorticography to manage mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy (MOGHE): a case report.
papers.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes a 25-year-old patient with MOGHE and refractory epilepsy, where SEEG and ECoG were combined to guide surgical resection. Despite a large resection, the patient experienced only occasional minor seizures after 14 months, suggesting that delayed diagnosis may lead to more extensive epileptogenic areas.

papers.title: Non-convulsive status epilepticus revealing acute deterioration in AARS2 mutation-associated progressive leukoencephalopathy.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 41-year-old woman with AARS2 mutation-associated progressive leukoencephalopathy who presented with non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) as the cause of acute clinical deterioration. EEG showed rhythmic frontal delta activity with sharp waves, and response to antiseizure treatment confirmed NCSE, highlighting the importance of considering NCSE in such patients with subacute neurological worsening.

papers.title: Electrical Signatures of Life: A Review of Cell Electrophysiology and Dielectric Analysis (2015-2026).
papers.summary: This review covers 2015-2026 literature on cell electrophysiology and dielectric analysis, focusing on label-free cellular electrical signatures (e.g., membrane capacitance, polarizability) and their applications in clinical diagnosis, drug development, and bioprocessing.

papers.title: Shielding the First 24 Postnatal Months of Life: A Proposal for a Prospective Cohort Study of Early-Life Electromagnetic Exposure and Autism Risk.
papers.summary: This protocol proposes a prospective cohort study to test whether reducing electromagnetic radiation exposure during the first 24 postnatal months, via sleep-phase Faraday shielding, can reduce autism risk, with exploratory genomic and EEG endpoints.

papers.title: Correction: Infra-slow EEG neurofeedback for insomnia: a single-case experimental study in primary care.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article on infra-slow EEG neurofeedback for insomnia. It corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fnhum.2026.1832178.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
